data.name: Holiday Bonus GOLD
data.detailed_description:
The best holiday match-3 game ever made is back! Now with 100% more levels! Holiday Bonus GOLD contains all the original levels from the classic version as well as 55 brand new levels for your delight. Pour yourself a glass of eggnog, grab a mince pie, and get stuck in.

Chill out with this cool winter-themed puzzle game from Grey Alien Games - it's slicker than Santa on an icy roof! Line up the dancing seasonal shapes against stunning snowscape backgrounds with an epic music score and work your way up the decorated tree.

You can gather winter scenes in your gallery and even display them on your desktop. Make the right moves and your power gauge will build a bigger, brighter bonus blowout!

This one's gonna snowball...so don't miss the festive fun!

Features:

  • Smooth, enjoyable match-3 gameplay.
  • Family holiday fun.
  • Crazy bonus items including Santa's sack!
  • 110 unique levels.
  • Beautiful winter backgrounds.
  • Enchanting winter music
  • Gallery of unlockable pictures.
  • Can set backgrounds as Desktop Wallpaper (PC only.)

Please Note: This game is not a mobile port. It was built for PC/Mac.

reviews.review:
[b]holiday bonus gold[/b] is your bog-standard match-3, and the christmas theme certainly doesn't help if you're a scrooge like me. don't get me wrong, there's some good festive stuff around, but this is nothing to write to santa about. still, I wanted to start at the beginning and sleigh my way through grey alien's match-3 catalog on steam.

this gold edition is from 2012 originally, the non-gold with 55 levels came out in 2006, which in turn was the follow-up to 2005's [b]xmas bonus[/b], so there's quite a bit of history. there are [b]110 levels[/b] here, half in the classic pack, the rest in the gold pack. both are unlocked from the start but levels within have to be completed one by one. [b]no move limit, mandatory timer, just measures time, doesn't count down[/b], and there's a hint button. matching is possible while animations are playing out, always nice.

[b]fun fact:[/b] levels are a bunch of text files, so it shouldn't be hard to create your own layouts.

power-ups aren't created or bought, but pre-placed on the levels and can be used when necessary, though there are more appearing later, so something must trigger them. some can be picked up and used on a tile of your choice, and if the thermometer charges up, the next power-up will be even more effective. it'd be useful if their explanations were part of the how to play section though, instead of a single pop-up when they're first introduced. as it is, by not paying too much attention, I ended up wasting a bunch of them. and it's worth noting that [b]most power-ups only destroy tokens and don't affect colored tiles behind them that have to be removed for completion[/b]. unfortunate.

graphics are functional, there's a details slider, a bunch of backgrounds you can set as wallpaper if you want a small image in the middle of the screen (the game runs in glorious 800x600 resolution), and further images to unlock in the gallery. [b]the song in the menu is abysmal[/b], think christmas music but disco. I swear it's wham's vomit-inducing [i]last christmas[/i], sans the singing (so it's a bit better). the rest is tolerable but still best if turned off. if you want matching music, I highly recommend the [b]trans-siberian orchestra[/b] christmas albums.

separate volume settings, custom cursor, windowed mode with a non-resizable and pretty small window by today's standards (again, 800x600), and there's a widescreen toggle, but it just stretches everything to fill the screen, doesn't look great.

it works as it should, so even though it's not something I felt like completing or even playing too much of, if you're looking for some yuletide match-3 action (or inaction) and don't mind the dated presentation, go for it, but wait for a sale.
